summary: The original is a sparse fire-ember pattern — a mostly-black strip crossed by a few bright red/orange streaks that zigzag and bounce — while the port's brightness ramps monotonically from 0 to saturation over ~3 s and then sits as a full-strip wash of railed yellow and pure green for the rest of the run.
observations: Neither side exposes any controls (meta.json controls list empty on both, probe reports 'no settable controls'); neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false both sides). No compile or runtime errors on either side.

Original steady state (60 px strip, survey 60 s @ 5 fps and late window --skip 40 @ 20 fps): meanBrightness avg ~21 (min 0, max 32), brightnessTrend steady, motion avg 12, zeroMotionFrames 1/300. The waterfall shows a black background with 2-4 bright streaks at any time, each travelling diagonally at roughly constant speed and reversing direction on a V-shaped kink — a 'shivering' bounce — leaving a short decaying tail behind it.

Port steady state over the same window: meanBrightness avg 160 (max 169), motion avg 0.6, zeroMotionFrames 246/300. The waterfall is a solid slab of saturated yellow from ~t=2 s to the end of the run; only the outermost 1-2 pixels at each strip end stay dark.

The port's runaway is monotonic, not a transient. stats.json meanBrightness for the port over the first 3 s at 20 fps: 0,0,1,3,9,17,24,31,37,40,40,40,40,40,40,41,...,132,...,163 — a one-way climb that never comes back down. The original's over the same frames oscillates: 0,0,0,1,...,26,25,26,25,27,...,31,30,30,29,...,12,11,11,10,17,17,15,15 — it rises and falls repeatedly, i.e. its heat term decays.
Extended to 240 s (--seconds 240 --fps 2) the port never recovers: mean 165, the whole waterfall is uniform yellow after the first couple of seconds. This is not a mode the pattern comes out of.

Colour is out of gamut, not merely too bright. --dump at t=45/47.5/50 s: original pixels are a smooth heat ramp with almost everything dim — [18,2,0], [100,0,0], [4,0,0] — punctuated by hotspots at [255,40,0] / [255,77,0]; meanB is exactly 0 across the whole run and meanG avg 7.7 (green only as the G component of orange). Port pixels at the same moments are hard-railed primaries: [0,255,0], [255,255,0], [255,0,0], nothing in between. Pure green (R=0, G=255) covers most of the strip in the late window and the original never produces it — the port's value has run past the end of the fire ramp and wrapped/clamped into hues the original's palette does not contain.
The port shows pure green within 0.5 s: pixels with G>128 at t=0.5/1/1.5/2/3 s are 12/15/32/45/57 of 60 on the port versus 0/0/0/4/0 on the original.

The port is not perfectly frozen — at 20 fps the late window shows saturated yellow and saturated green plateaus with boundaries creeping a few pixels per second — but at the survey rate 82% of frames register zero motion, and the visible result is a static wash rather than an animation.
The divergence is seed-independent: at --seed 1234 the original renders the same sparse bouncing-streak character (mean 20, motion 11) and the port the same saturated wash (mean 161, motion 1).

The port's earliest ~0.4 s is superficially plausible (both sides start black and brighten from a couple of seeds), but it is already 7x too bright at t=0.25 s (17.1 vs 2.3) and never resembles the original after that.
feedback: The port has a runaway accumulator with no decay term — the same failure class as the sibling aurorashivers port. Its per-pixel heat value only ever increases, so mean brightness climbs 0 -> 163 in about 3 s and pins there for at least 240 s. Whatever quantity is being integrated needs a per-frame cooling/decay applied every frame, sized so that mean strip brightness oscillates in the ~10-32 range indefinitely instead of climbing.

Target behaviour to reproduce: a black strip with only 2-4 bright features alive at once. Each feature is a compact hot spot ~3-6 px wide that travels along the strip at a steady speed, reverses direction after a while (the waterfall shows clean V kinks, not smooth sine turnarounds), and drags a short trail that fades to black within roughly a second. Roughly 40-50% of pixels are at or near zero at any instant.

Clamp or wrap the palette lookup so the heat value cannot run past the end of the fire ramp. The original's gamut is strictly black -> dark red -> orange -> yellow-white: blue is exactly 0 on every pixel of every frame, and green only ever appears alongside a large red (e.g. [255,40,0]). The port emits [0,255,0] — pure green with zero red — across most of the strip, which means the index is overrunning the ramp. Saturating the index at the hot end of the fire palette would at worst give white-hot pixels rather than green ones.

Do not tune this by lowering an overall brightness scale. The problem is dynamic range collapse, not gain: the port's pixels are quantized to 0 or 255 per channel with nothing in between, while the original's histogram is dominated by dim values (single- and double-digit reds). Restoring the decay should restore the intermediate values by itself.

Check the motion/agitation term separately once decay is fixed. The original's streaks move at a visibly constant px/frame and bounce; the port shows no travelling features at all at any point, so it is not yet possible to tell from output whether the port's motion logic is also wrong or merely buried under the saturation. Re-verify motion after the decay fix.

Sanity target for a future run: over a 60 s / 5 fps capture the port should post meanBrightness avg near 21 with brightnessTrend steady, motion avg around 12, and zeroMotionFrames of 1 — currently it posts 160 / steady / 0.6 / 246.
